difficultyReason: Single causal claim with one obvious alternative explanation. The stimulus argues that a policy caused a specific outcome; the correct answer introduces a straightforward confounding variable that occurred at the same time.
stimulus: After City Council approved a new traffic-reduction initiative in March, traffic congestion in downtown declined by 20% over the following six months. Clearly, the traffic-reduction initiative was responsible for the decrease in congestion.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The traffic-reduction initiative was supported by environmental groups.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A major employer relocated out of downtown in April, significantly reducing the number of commuters in the area.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Traffic congestion typically decreases during the summer months.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Other cities have implemented similar traffic-reduction initiatives with mixed results.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The City Council had previously considered and rejected a traffic-reduction initiative five years earlier.

explanations.correct: B introduces an alternative explanation for the observed decrease in congestion. If a major employer relocated out of downtown in April—shortly after the initiative was approved—that relocation could fully account for the 20% reduction, undermining the claim that the initiative itself was responsible.
explanations.A: Accurate but irrelevant. The source of support for the initiative does not address whether it actually caused the congestion reduction.
explanations.C: Weakens the argument only marginally and does not establish a competing causal explanation. Seasonal variation is a general pattern; it does not show that this specific reduction was caused by something other than the initiative.
explanations.D: Out of scope. The success or failure of similar initiatives in other cities does not speak to whether this initiative caused the downtown reduction.
explanations.E: Irrelevant. A previous rejected proposal has no bearing on whether the March initiative caused the congestion decrease.

difficultyReason: Straightforward causal overreach. A single temporal correlation (two events coincide) is mistaken for causation. The correct answer offers an obvious alternative cause.
stimulus: Dr. Chen observed that patients who took a new herbal supplement reported fewer migraines in the week following their first dose. Therefore, the supplement directly reduces migraine frequency.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously undermines Dr. Chen's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Some patients reported that they felt optimistic about the supplement's efficacy before taking their first dose.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Migraine frequency naturally varies week to week, and many patients experience spontaneous improvement regardless of any treatment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The supplement contains several ingredients that are known to aid digestion.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Other herbal supplements have been shown to reduce migraines in some patients.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Dr. Chen also studied the effects of the supplement on other common ailments such as insomnia and joint pain.

explanations.correct: B provides an alternative explanation for the observed improvement. If migraines naturally fluctuate and patients often experience spontaneous remission, the reported reduction may have nothing to do with the supplement. This directly undermines the causal claim.
explanations.A: Introduces placebo effect, which, though relevant to medical efficacy, is more of a strengthener (shows the supplement works through some mechanism). Does not establish an alternative explanation.
explanations.C: Accurate but irrelevant. The supplement's digestive properties do not address whether it causes migraine reduction.
explanations.D: Out of scope. Other supplements' efficacy does not speak to whether this supplement caused the migraine reduction in Dr. Chen's observation.
explanations.E: Irrelevant. Studying side effects or applications to other conditions does not weaken the claim about migraines.

difficultyReason: Simple predictive or causal argument where a single factor is claimed to drive a result. The correct answer shows that the result can occur without that factor, or that the factor is absent when the result occurs.
stimulus: After the museum installed interactive displays featuring touchscreen technology, visitor attendance increased by 30% within three months. The museum director concluded that the interactive displays were the primary reason for the surge in attendance.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The interactive displays were designed by a team of experienced technology consultants.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A major news outlet ran a feature story about the museum's renovation project one week after the displays were installed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Touchscreen technology has become increasingly affordable for museums in recent years.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Similar museums in other regions have not experienced comparable attendance increases.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The museum's admission price remained unchanged during the three-month period.

explanations.correct: B introduces an alternative explanation for the attendance surge. The major news story could have independently driven the 30% increase. This undercuts the director's attribution of the surge solely to the interactive displays.
explanations.A: Accurate but irrelevant. The credentials of the designers do not address whether the displays caused the attendance increase.
explanations.C: Out of scope. General trends in touchscreen pricing do not explain why attendance rose at this particular museum.
explanations.D: Introduces a comparative that weakens by disanalogy, but does not rule out that the displays caused the increase at this museum.
explanations.E: Irrelevant. Stable pricing does not address what caused the attendance boost.
